description:
## Problem

`use_event_ref` handlers are plain closures called by `invoke_event_handler/3` in `Filament.LiveView`. Currently all handler arities (0-arity and 1-arity) discard their return value and the socket is never surfaced:

```elixir
defp invoke_event_handler(fun, _params, socket) when is_function(fun, 0) do
  fun.()
  {:noreply, socket}   # handler return value discarded
end

defp invoke_event_handler(fun, params, socket) when is_function(fun, 1) do
  fun.(params)
  {:noreply, socket}   # handler return value discarded
end
```

This means a `use_event_ref` handler has no way to push events back to the client — `Phoenix.LiveView.push_event/3` requires the socket, which is never made available.

## Why This Matters

The use case that drives this is JS hooks that use `this.handleEvent` to receive server-initiated commands: imperative actions (splicing text into a textarea, resetting a form field) that cannot be expressed as rendered HTML. Three concrete blocked cases from the consumer app:

- **`pop_queued_last`** — pops a queued prompt entry from an OTP process, then must push `set_prompt_text` so the `PromptInput` JS hook splices the text back into the textarea.
- **`picker_select` / `picker_select_at`** — resolve the selected picker item, then must push `picker_accept` so the JS hook splices the accepted value into the cursor position.
- **`annotate_line`** — writes an annotation to a `ReviewServer`, then must push `annotation_added` so the `DiffAnnotate` hook resets the inline form.

Without this, all three handlers must live in the root `handle_event/3` callback of the LiveView rather than in the component that owns the state and the OTP call.

## Proposed API

The simplest fix is a 2-arity handler form where the second argument is the live socket, and Filament uses the returned socket:

```elixir
defp invoke_event_handler(fun, params, socket) when is_function(fun, 2) do
  case fun.(params, socket) do
    {:noreply, socket} -> {:noreply, socket}
    socket             -> {:noreply, socket}
  end
end
```

Usage at the call site:

```elixir
import Filament.Experimental.Hooks

accept_ref = use_event_ref(fn %{"value" => v}, socket ->
  do_something(v)
  {:noreply, Phoenix.LiveView.push_event(socket, "picker_accept", %{value: v})}
end)
```

### Alternative: explicit push side-channel

If passing the raw socket feels too low-level or leaky, an alternative is a scoped push helper injected by Filament:

```elixir
accept_ref = use_event_ref(fn %{"value" => v}, push ->
  do_something(v)
  push.("picker_accept", %{value: v})
end)
```

where `push` is a closure Filament constructs over the socket internally — the handler never touches the socket directly. This keeps the component API socket-free while still allowing push_event semantics.

## Notes

- The 2-arity form is additive and backward-compatible: existing 0-arity and 1-arity handlers continue to work unchanged.
- The `use_event_ref` CHANGELOG entry in 0.4.0 already notes the handler receives the payload — extending it to optionally receive a socket (or push helper) is a natural progression.
- This does not affect `on_*` attribute handlers (those run inside the render pass and have no need for push_event since re-render handles state changes). It is purely a `use_event_ref`-level concern.
title: use_event_ref handlers should be able to push events to the client
